== plugins/agent-workflows/skills/do-task/SKILL.md ==
---
name: do-task
description: |
  Does the work a claimed issue describes — writes and commits the change, or performs the
  act and captures the evidence that it happened. Holds the scope the issue set, records
  why in the commit message rather than only what, and ends by stating what state the work
  is actually in rather than declaring it done. The write half of an issue; something else
  judges whether it finished.
when_to_use: |
  Use once an issue is claimed and the work should start, whatever kind it is — "implement
  it", "fix it", "make the change", "go ahead", "do it". Code: "write the parser fix".
  Docs: "update that README". Environment: "run the staging upgrade". Operations: "rotate
  the cert now", "run the migration", "restart it". Reach for it after take-issue has
  claimed something, and when the user says do it on work already understood. Not for
  choosing what to work on, not for opening a change request, and not for deciding whether
  the result is good enough — each of those is somebody else's job.
argument-hint: "[issue-number]"
---

# Do the task
== plugins/agent-workflows/skills/file-issue/SKILL.md ==
---
name: file-issue
description: |
  Turns something said in a session into a tracked issue that a cold agent can act on, and
  copies the session log beside it wherever one can be had — always attempted, never a

content.content:
---
name: setup-agent-workflows
description: |
  Adopts the agent-workflows plugin into a project — writes the profile sections these
  units resolve against, binds the report contract in CLAUDE.md, and finds the forked
  copies of retired commands that silently shadow the placed ones. Use before the first
  run of ship-create-pr, ship-merge, gen-readme or the reviewing skills, when a unit
  stops because it cannot resolve a project value, or when migrating a repo that holds
  `dw-*` / `qw-*` forks.
---

# Setup agent-workflows

**Placement puts the units where an agent loads them. This is the other half — adoption.**
The placed units describe *some* project; this makes them describe *this* one. It runs once
per repo, and again only to change an answer.

Three things, and the third is the one nobody expects to need:

- **Profile values** — the sections these units resolve against, so no unit stops on an
  unresolvable value
- **The report contract binding** — a line in `CLAUDE.md` that holds every session, rather
  than waiting for a skill to invoke itself
- **Fork migration** — the local copies of retired commands that still appear in the menu
  with nothing announcing which one ran

This is prompt-driven, not a script. Explore, present what you found, confirm, then write.

## It writes only what this plugin owns

A project may place several plugins that all read one `project-profile.md`. The rules are
in `profile-doctrine.md` → "More than one plugin writes this file", and they bind here:
own only what you read, add or update in place and never truncate, and treat a value
already there as a decision rather than something to overwrite.

The sections this plugin owns, and nothing else:
**Labels · Linking & branch · Platform · Git · Docs & diagrams · Reports · Review

content.content:
# Forked units: what each one became

A project that used this toolkit before it was a plugin holds copies of its units under
`.claude/commands/` or `.claude/skills/`. Those copies still work, still appear in the
menu, and are the reason a migration needs a document at all.

**The trap.** A fork is silently newer or older than what is placed, and nothing surfaces
the conflict. A local `dw-story.md` and the plugin's units coexist under different
namespaces, so both appear and neither announces the other. Nobody is told which one ran.

**Telling them apart while both exist.** Every unit this plugin ships is a skill, so it
answers to a namespaced name as well as a bare one. `/agent-workflows:ship-merge` always
reaches the placed unit; `/ship-merge` reaches a local fork of that name instead, when one
is there. Until the fork is gone, the namespaced form is the only one that says which copy
ran.

## The mapping

**Renamed** — the unit survived under a new name. The fork is redundant; delete it and
type the new name.

| Forked unit | Became |
|---|---|
| `dw-create-pr` | `ship-create-pr` (this plugin) |
| `dw-merge` | `ship-merge` (this plugin) |
| `qw-plan`, `qw-cases`, `qw-review-plan`, `qw-review-cases` | `qa-*` in **`agent-workflows-runner`** — a different plugin, placed separately |
| `auditing-artifacts`, `auditing-readme` | `reviewing-artifacts`, `reviewing-phrasing`, `reviewing-typography` (this plugin) |

**Deleted, not renamed** — this is the distinction easiest to get wrong. Nothing here has
a new name to type; the authoring half is no longer this plugin's.

| Forked unit | What replaces it |
|---|---|
| `dw-story`, `dw-plan`, `dw-tasks`, `dw-implement` | nothing here — the build half is out of scope |
| `dw-review-story`, `dw-review-tasks`, `dw-review-implement`, `dw-review-pr` | nothing — a diff review plus `reviewing-finish` cover it |
| `dw-test-design` | the runner's `qa-*` half |
| `qw-drift` | **nothing.** See the consequence below. |

**Rules** — these ship from the plugins now. A local copy of any of them drifts from the
one the units actually read.

| Forked rule | Ships from |
|---|---|
| `rules/agent-report.md`, `rules/profile-doctrine.md`, `rules/anti-slop.md` | this plugin |
| `rules/ship-tail.md`, `rules/doc-workflow.md` | this plugin |
| `rules/dev-workflow.md` | deleted with the pipeline it described |
| `rules/qa-workflow.md` | `agent-workflows-runner` |

**Keep.** `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` stays in the project — it is the values half
and it is the one file adoption edits. What changed is that its **doctrine preamble** now
ships as `profile-doctrine.md`; a project holding the old combined file should keep its
values and let the preamble shrink to the pointer, or the two drift.

## Consequences a project cannot anticipate

Say these out loud before removing anything — they are the reason this is a conversation
and not a delete loop.

- **`qw-drift` has no replacement.** Removing it orphans the project's drift tooling and
  whatever front-matter anchor that tooling read. If the project depends on drift
  detection, it keeps the fork or rebuilds it as a project-owned unit; nothing in either
  plugin will do it.
- **A local `project-profile.md` may be missing keys the surviving units read**, and may
  still carry the old combined form where the doctrine preamble sat inline. Keep its
  values; let the preamble shrink to the pointer, or the shipped `profile-doctrine.md` and
  the inline copy drift apart with nothing saying which one a unit followed.
- **The runner's units are a separate placement.** Deleting `qw-*` without placing
  `agent-workflows-runner` leaves the project with no QA half at all, not a renamed one.

## Telling what is actually placed

A fork is only redundant if the plugin's copy is really there, and the obvious way to
check is misleading.

`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` pins an `installPath` into a cache snapshot
that may be many commits stale — and on a **directory**-source marketplace that snapshot
is not what loads at all. Read `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json` first:

- `"source": "directory"` — the working tree at that path is what loads. Read the units
  there; a restart picks up uncommitted edits.
- `"source": "github"` — a snapshot pinned to a commit. `claude plugin update
  <plugin>@<marketplace>` moves it, and the commit is the version; there is no number to
  compare.

Qualify the name with the marketplace when updating — the bare plugin name does not
resolve.

**DONE** — `.sessions/` synced: 6 transcripts, all byte-identical to source (1 new, 1 refreshed, 4 already current).
**REVISE** — `setup-agent-workflows` is not merely stale on names: the values layer it exists to write was abandoned by the redesign.
Next: leave it for the later pass — nothing to run now.

---

### 1 · Sessions saved

| Session | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `f4492b01` | stale — 4.48 MB of 5.92 | refreshed, verbatim |
| `da3e9fe4` (this one) | absent | added — snapshot at copy time, still live |
| 4 others + subagent dirs | current | untouched |

Copied whole, not rendered; `memory/` excluded. Verified by md5 per file.

### 2 · The goal of `setup-agent-workflows`

It claims three jobs. One survives the redesign intact.

| # | Job as written | Still real? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the `project-profile.md` sections units resolve against | **No.** The shipped units carry their own defaults and derive the platform from `git remote` |
| 2 | Bind the report contract in `CLAUDE.md` | **Partly.** The binding text points at `rules/agent-report.md` — the plugin ships no `rules/` directory at all |
| 3 | Find forked copies that silently shadow placed units | **Yes.** This half still has a job, and nothing else does it |

```
DESIGNED (values indirection)          SHIPPED (defaults inline)
  unit ──reads──► project-profile.md     unit ──carries──► Values table w/ default
                        ▲                                        │
                setup writes it                    overridden by ▼  the project,
                                                       where it declares one
                                       platform ──derived at run time──► git remote
```

**Restated goal:** make a project's copy of the toolkit unambiguous — one copy of each unit, and a stated override only where a unit's default is wrong for that project. Not a profile-writing step.

### 3 · Guideline for the legacy files

| Class | Test | Treatment | Instances here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 · Renamed | the job survives under a new name | retype the name | `ship-create-pr`→`open-pr`, `ship-merge`→`land-pr`, `reviewing-finish`→`review-work`, `doc-gen-readme`→`gen-readme`, `doc-review-readme`→`review-readme` |
| 2 · Deleted | no successor ships | delete the sentence — never rename into a guess | `rules/agent-report.md`, `profile-doctrine.md`, `ship-tail.md`, `doc-workflow.md`, `dev-workflow.md`, `anti-slop.md` |
| 3 · Superseded | the *mechanism* lost, not the file | rewrite the section, not the reference | `project-profile.md` — 7 citations |
| 4 · Foreign | names something outside this repo | verify it exists before citing | `agent-workflows-runner`, `setup-agent-runner`, `dw-*`, `qw-*`, `qa-*` |

```
a legacy name
     │
     ├─ inside .sessions/ ? ──yes──► leave it. The log is a record,
     │                                not a reference. Never edited.
     no
     ▼
 does the job still ship, under any name? ──yes──► rename        (1)
     │ no
     ▼
 replaced by a different mechanism?       ──yes──► rewrite       (3)
     │ no
     ▼
 does the named thing exist at all?       ──yes──► cite exactly  (4)
     │ no
     ▼
   delete the sentence                                           (2)
```

**Two rules the classes rest on.** Class 2 is the one that goes wrong: a deleted mechanism has no new name, so renaming it invents a promise. And the archive is out of scope by design — `check-refs.sh` currently counts it, so 2,604 of its 2,649 hits are `.sessions/` and `tmp/` lines burying the 45 that are real (43 in the setup skill, 1 in `plugin.json`, 1 in `marketplace.json`).

# Reworking the adoption unit — plan

Companion to `redesign-draft.md`, which is the design record for the six workflow units and
is not edited by this file. This one covers the seventh unit, the one the draft never had a
row for: `setup-agent-workflows`.

Last updated 2026-08-16.

## 1. Why it needs a rework, not a rename

The unit was built around an indirection the redesign removed.

```
DESIGNED (values indirection)              SHIPPED (defaults inline)
  unit ──reads──► project-profile.md         unit ──carries──► Values table + default
                        ▲                                            │
                setup writes the sections            overridden by   ▼   the project,
                                                          where it declares one
                                           platform ──derived at run time──► git remote
```

Its three stated jobs, against what shipped:

| # | Job as written | Still real? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the `project-profile.md` sections units resolve against | **No, for our units** | `gen-readme`, `open-pr`, `land-pr` and the rest state their own defaults and say the project's declaration wins |
| 2 | Bind the report contract in `CLAUDE.md` | **Broken as written** | The block it inserts cites `rules/agent-report.md`; this plugin ships no `rules/` directory |
| 3 | Find forked copies that shadow placed units | **Yes** | Confirmed live — see §3 |

**Restated goal.** Make a project's copy of the toolkit unambiguous: one copy of each unit,
and a stated override only where a unit's default is wrong for that project. Not a
profile-writing step.

Rename follows the restated goal and is decided last, once §2 and §3 are settled — the
name should describe the job that survives, and that job is not final yet.

## 2. Legacy artifacts — the evaluation

The recommendation on the table is *remove the story files and rule files*. Evaluated one
by one. Three agree, two do not.

| Artifact | Where | Recommendation | Verdict | The cost of the wrong call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/stories/` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done** at `8f47b2b`. Nothing writes or reads one | none |
| `plugins/**/rules/*.md` (5 files) | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** Each skill now carries its doctrine inline; a cited file with one reader rots unnoticed | none |
| `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** This repo declares no overrides | none |
| `templates/CLAUDE.md` | this repo | — | **CUT — byte-identical to the repo's own `CLAUDE.md`** after the staged edit. Two copies, one reader, no rule saying which is authoritative | a template that drifts from the file it was copied from |
| **the profile as a concept, in an adopter** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — keep the file, drop our sections** | §2.1 |
| **the `CLAUDE.md` binding** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — replace, do not delete** | §2.2 |

### 2.1 The profile file survives us

Our six units no longer read it. `agent-workflows-runner` still does — it is placed from
`~/src/test-framework-template`, ships six `qa-*` commands plus `setup-agent-runner`, and
resolves `Paths`, `Reports`, `Connected flow` and its binding layer out of that same file.

| If we… | Then |
|---|---|
| delete the file from adopters | the runner's commands stop on an unresolvable value |
| keep writing our seven sections | we maintain a values layer nothing of ours reads |
| **stop owning sections, leave the file alone** | both plugins hold; ours use defaults, the runner keeps its own half |

There is one loose end either way. Every unit says *"the project's declaration wins"* without
naming where a declaration lives. Removing the file with no replacement leaves that sentence
unresolvable — the promise has to point somewhere, and `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` is
already the somewhere for the other plugin.

### 2.2 The binding is broken, not unnecessary

The `CLAUDE.md` block cites `rules/agent-report.md` and `project-profile.md → Reports`.
Neither ships here. So the current binding is dead text and must not stay as written.

But the argument for having one is in `reporting-outcomes` itself: *an agent producing a
muddled report is the least likely thing to notice it is producing one.* A skill that must
recognise its own failure to trigger is the case the binding exists for.

| Option | Keeps the guard | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A · delete the binding | no — relies on the skill's own description firing | zero maintenance; the failure mode is silent |
| B · **replace it with one line naming the skill**, no `rules/` citation | yes | one section written into an adopter's `CLAUDE.md` |
| C · keep as written | no — cites two files that do not exist | dead reference |

**Lean: B.** It is the smallest thing that still fires without self-invocation.

## 3. The forks are real

Not hypothetical. The sibling repo holds live copies of units this plugin ships:

| Fork found in `~/src/test-framework-template` | Class | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/reviewing-artifacts`, `reviewing-phrasing`, `reviewing-typography` | shadows a placed unit | the case §3 of the unit exists for |
| `.claude/commands/dw-test-design.md` | deleted, not renamed | the runner's `qa-*` half replaces it |
| `.claude/rules/agent-report.md`, `project-profile.md` | the runner's, not ours | leave alone |

So `fork-migration.md` keeps its job; its mapping table is what goes stale, not its reason
for existing.

## 4. Handling a legacy name — the rule the rework follows

```
a legacy name
     │
     ├─ inside .sessions/ ? ──yes──► leave it. The log is a record,
     │                                not a reference. Never edited.
     no
     ▼
 does the job still ship, under any name? ──yes──► rename        (1)
     │ no
     ▼
 replaced by a different mechanism?       ──yes──► rewrite       (3)
     │ no
     ▼
 does the named thing exist anywhere?     ──yes──► cite exactly  (4)
     │ no
     ▼
   delete the sentence                                           (2)
```

| Class | Instances |
|---|---|
| 1 · Renamed | `ship-create-pr`→`open-pr`, `ship-merge`→`land-pr`, `reviewing-finish`→`review-work`, `doc-gen-readme`→`gen-readme`, `doc-review-readme`→`review-readme` |
| 2 · Deleted | `rules/agent-report.md`, `profile-doctrine.md`, `ship-tail.md`, `doc-workflow.md`, `dev-workflow.md`, `anti-slop.md` — *in this repo*; the runner still holds its own `agent-report.md` |
| 3 · Superseded | `project-profile.md` — 7 citations, and see §2.1 |
| 4 · Foreign but real | `agent-workflows-runner`, `setup-agent-runner`, `qa-*`, `dw-*`, `qw-*` — verified present in the sibling repo, so these cite correctly |

**Class 2 is the one that goes wrong.** A deleted mechanism has no new name, so renaming it
invents a promise. Delete the sentence instead.

## 5. Open items

Nothing here is decided. Ordered by what blocks what.

| # | Item | Blocks | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Profile: stop owning sections but leave the file, or drop it entirely | B, D | stop owning; leave it (§2.1) |
| B | `CLAUDE.md` binding: delete, or replace with a one-line pointer | D | replace (§2.2) |
| C | `check-refs.sh`: exclude `.sessions/` and `tmp/` | the rewrite's verify step | exclude — 2,604 of 2,649 hits are archive lines burying the 45 real ones |
| D | The rename, once A and B fix what the unit's job actually is | — | decide at the end of the session, per your call |
| E | `fork-migration.md`: rewrite the mapping to current names, keep the doc | D | keep, rewrite |
| F | `plugin.json` + `marketplace.json` descriptions still sell the old unit set | — | rewrite with the rename, one commit |
| G | `templates/CLAUDE.md` is now a duplicate of `CLAUDE.md` | — | cut |
| H | Cross-plugin: does the runner's `setup-agent-runner` need to know our sections went away | A | tell it, do not edit it — the sibling repo is not ours to sync |
| I | `redesign-draft.md` is stale on 5 of 7 rows — supersede it or annotate it | — | leave it; it is a record. This file carries current state |
| J | Session logs: copying is manual today; nothing automates it | — | leave manual until it bites |
| K | Draft's open question B — 13 MB of logs across 6 sessions, workability unknown | — | still open, only running it tells |

## 6. Build order

1. **C** — fix `check-refs.sh` first; it is the verify step for everything after it
2. **A, B** — settle what the unit still does, which is what makes the rewrite writable
3. **Rewrite `SKILL.md` + `profile-sections.md` + `fork-migration.md`** against §4
4. **D** — rename, and move the directory
5. **F, G** — descriptions and the duplicate template, in the rename's commit
6. Verify: `scripts/check-refs.sh` reports clean outside `.sessions/`

# Reworking the adoption unit — plan

Companion to `redesign-draft.md`, which is the design record for the six workflow units and
is not edited by this file. This one covers the seventh unit, the one the draft never had a
row for: `setup-agent-workflows`.

Last updated 2026-08-16.

## 1. Why it needs a rework, not a rename

The unit was built around an indirection the redesign removed.

```
DESIGNED (values indirection)              SHIPPED (defaults inline)
  unit ──reads──► project-profile.md         unit ──carries──► Values table + default
                        ▲                                            │
                setup writes the sections            overridden by   ▼   the project,
                                                          where it declares one
                                           platform ──derived at run time──► git remote
```

Its three stated jobs, against what shipped:

| # | Job as written | Still real? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the `project-profile.md` sections units resolve against | **No, for our units** | `gen-readme`, `open-pr`, `land-pr` and the rest state their own defaults and say the project's declaration wins |
| 2 | Bind the report contract in `CLAUDE.md` | **Broken as written** | The block it inserts cites `rules/agent-report.md`; this plugin ships no `rules/` directory |
| 3 | Find forked copies that shadow placed units | **Yes** | Confirmed live — see §3 |

**Restated goal.** Make a project's copy of the toolkit unambiguous: one copy of each unit,
and a stated override only where a unit's default is wrong for that project. Not a
profile-writing step.

Rename follows the restated goal and is decided last, once §2 and §3 are settled — the
name should describe the job that survives, and that job is not final yet.

## 2. Legacy artifacts — the evaluation

The recommendation on the table is *remove the story files and rule files*. Evaluated one
by one. Three agree, two do not.

| Artifact | Where | Recommendation | Verdict | The cost of the wrong call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/stories/` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done** at `8f47b2b`. Nothing writes or reads one | none |
| `plugins/**/rules/*.md` (5 files) | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** Each skill now carries its doctrine inline; a cited file with one reader rots unnoticed | none |
| `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** This repo declares no overrides | none |
| `templates/CLAUDE.md` | this repo | — | **CUT — byte-identical to the repo's own `CLAUDE.md`** after the staged edit. Two copies, one reader, no rule saying which is authoritative | a template that drifts from the file it was copied from |
| **the profile as a concept, in an adopter** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — keep the file, drop our sections** | §2.1 |
| **the `CLAUDE.md` binding** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — replace, do not delete** | §2.2 |

### 2.1 The profile file survives us

Our six units no longer read it. `agent-workflows-runner` still does — it is placed from
`~/src/test-framework-template`, ships six `qa-*` commands plus `setup-agent-runner`, and
resolves `Paths`, `Reports`, `Connected flow` and its binding layer out of that same file.

| If we… | Then |
|---|---|
| delete the file from adopters | the runner's commands stop on an unresolvable value |
| keep writing our seven sections | we maintain a values layer nothing of ours reads |
| **stop owning sections, leave the file alone** | both plugins hold; ours use defaults, the runner keeps its own half |

There is one loose end either way. Every unit says *"the project's declaration wins"* without
naming where a declaration lives. Removing the file with no replacement leaves that sentence
unresolvable — the promise has to point somewhere, and `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` is
already the somewhere for the other plugin.

### 2.2 The binding is broken, not unnecessary

The `CLAUDE.md` block cites `rules/agent-report.md` and `project-profile.md → Reports`.
Neither ships here. So the current binding is dead text and must not stay as written.

But the argument for having one is in `reporting-outcomes` itself: *an agent producing a
muddled report is the least likely thing to notice it is producing one.* A skill that must
recognise its own failure to trigger is the case the binding exists for.

| Option | Keeps the guard | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A · delete the binding | no — relies on the skill's own description firing | zero maintenance; the failure mode is silent |
| B · **replace it with one line naming the skill**, no `rules/` citation | yes | one section written into an adopter's `CLAUDE.md` |
| C · keep as written | no — cites two files that do not exist | dead reference |

**Lean: B.** It is the smallest thing that still fires without self-invocation.

## 3. The forks are real

Not hypothetical. The sibling repo holds live copies of units this plugin ships:

| Fork found in `~/src/test-framework-template` | Class | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/skills/reviewing-artifacts`, `reviewing-phrasing`, `reviewing-typography` | shadows a placed unit | the case §3 of the unit exists for |
| `.claude/commands/dw-test-design.md` | deleted, not renamed | the runner's `qa-*` half replaces it |
| `.claude/rules/agent-report.md`, `project-profile.md` | the runner's, not ours | leave alone |

So `fork-migration.md` keeps its job; its mapping table is what goes stale, not its reason
for existing.

## 4. Handling a legacy name — the rule the rework follows

```
a legacy name
     │
     ├─ inside .sessions/ ? ──yes──► leave it. The log is a record,
     │                                not a reference. Never edited.
     no
     ▼
 does the job still ship, under any name? ──yes──► rename        (1)
     │ no
     ▼
 replaced by a different mechanism?       ──yes──► rewrite       (3)
     │ no
     ▼
 does the named thing exist anywhere?     ──yes──► cite exactly  (4)
     │ no
     ▼
   delete the sentence                                           (2)
```

| Class | Instances |
|---|---|
| 1 · Renamed | `ship-create-pr`→`open-pr`, `ship-merge`→`land-pr`, `reviewing-finish`→`review-work`, `doc-gen-readme`→`gen-readme`, `doc-review-readme`→`review-readme` |
| 2 · Deleted | `rules/agent-report.md`, `profile-doctrine.md`, `ship-tail.md`, `doc-workflow.md`, `dev-workflow.md`, `anti-slop.md` — *in this repo*; the runner still holds its own `agent-report.md` |
| 3 · Superseded | `project-profile.md` — 7 citations, and see §2.1 |
| 4 · Foreign but real | `agent-workflows-runner`, `setup-agent-runner`, `qa-*`, `dw-*`, `qw-*` — verified present in the sibling repo, so these cite correctly |

**Class 2 is the one that goes wrong.** A deleted mechanism has no new name, so renaming it
invents a promise. Delete the sentence instead.

## 5. Open items

Nothing here is decided. Ordered by what blocks what.

| # | Item | Blocks | Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Profile: stop owning sections but leave the file, or drop it entirely | B, D | stop owning; leave it (§2.1) |
| B | `CLAUDE.md` binding: delete, or replace with a one-line pointer | D | replace (§2.2) |
| C | `check-refs.sh`: exclude `.sessions/` and `tmp/` | the rewrite's verify step | exclude — 2,604 of 2,649 hits are archive lines burying the 45 real ones |
| D | The rename, once A and B fix what the unit's job actually is | — | decide at the end of the session, per your call |
| E | `fork-migration.md`: rewrite the mapping to current names, keep the doc | D | keep, rewrite |
| F | `plugin.json` + `marketplace.json` descriptions still sell the old unit set | — | rewrite with the rename, one commit |
| G | `templates/CLAUDE.md` is now a duplicate of `CLAUDE.md` | — | cut |
| H | Cross-plugin: does the runner's `setup-agent-runner` need to know our sections went away | A | tell it, do not edit it — the sibling repo is not ours to sync |
| I | `redesign-draft.md` is stale on 5 of 7 rows — supersede it or annotate it | — | leave it; it is a record. This file carries current state |
| J | Session logs: copying is manual today; nothing automates it | — | leave manual until it bites |
| K | Draft's open question B — 13 MB of logs across 6 sessions, workability unknown | — | still open, only running it tells |

## 6. Build order

1. **C** — fix `check-refs.sh` first; it is the verify step for everything after it
2. **A, B** — settle what the unit still does, which is what makes the rewrite writable
3. **Rewrite `SKILL.md` + `profile-sections.md` + `fork-migration.md`** against §4
4. **D** — rename, and move the directory
5. **F, G** — descriptions and the duplicate template, in the rename's commit
6. Verify: `scripts/check-refs.sh` reports clean outside `.sessions/`

content.content:
1	# READMEs and Project Docs
2	
3	## Contents
4	
5	- What a README is for
6	- Standard structure
7	- The first screen
8	- Installation and configuration
9	- Usage examples
10	- What belongs elsewhere
11	- Contributing guides
12	- Changelogs
13	- Review checklist
14	
15	## What a README is for
16	
17	A README answers four questions for someone who arrived from a search result and will leave in thirty seconds if unsatisfied:
18	
19	1. What is this?
20	2. Do I want it?
21	3. How do I run it?
22	4. Where do I go next?
23	
24	It is not a manual. Every paragraph that does not serve one of those four questions pushes the answers below the fold.
25	
26	## Standard structure
27	
28	```
29	# project-name
30	
31	<one-sentence description>
32	
33	<badges — optional, and only informative ones: build, version, license>
34	
35	## What it does
36	## Requirements
37	## Installation
38	## Quick start
39	## Configuration
40	## Documentation  (links out)
41	## Contributing
42	## License
43	```
44	
45	Reorder only for a reason. Readers scan for these headings by habit, and unfamiliar organization costs them time.
46	
47	## The first screen
48	
49	The single most valuable line is the description directly under the title. It must be concrete and complete without context:
50	
51	> An MCP server exposing TestLink test case management to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol.
52	
53	Not:
54	
55	> A powerful, flexible tool for modern test workflows.
56	
57	Marketing adjectives — powerful, seamless, blazing fast, modern, simple — carry no information and signal that the author had nothing specific to say. Delete them all.
58	
59	Follow the description with what the project does in three to six bullets, each naming a real capability. Then reach a runnable command as fast as possible. If a reader cannot execute something within the first screen, the README is too slow.
60	
61	Badge rows exceeding four items become noise. Keep build status, version, and license; drop the rest.
62	
63	## Installation and configuration
64	
65	State prerequisites with versions before the install command, so a reader fails fast rather than midway:
66	
67	```
68	Requires Python 3.11+, and a TestLink instance with the XML-RPC API enabled.
69	```
70	
71	Give one canonical install path. Alternatives (source build, container, package manager variants) go below the canonical one, clearly subordinate. Presenting three equal options forces a decision the reader is not equipped to make.
72	
73	Document configuration as a table, since readers arrive looking for one specific key:
74	
75	| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| `TESTLINK_URL` | Yes | — | Base URL of the TestLink XML-RPC endpoint |
78	| `TESTLINK_API_KEY` | Yes | — | Personal API key from user settings |
79	| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | No | `30` | Seconds before an API call aborts |
80	
81	Never put a real credential in an example, even an expired one.
82	
83	## Usage examples
84	
85	Two or three examples, ordered by frequency of use, not by complexity. The first must be the thing almost everyone does.
86	
87	Each example shows the invocation and its output:
88	
89	```bash
90	testcase-validator check --project TestLink-QA --file cases.json
91	```
92	
93	```
94	Validated 47 cases. 2 rejected:
95	  case_12: field 'importance' = 'critical' (expected: 1, 2, 3)
96	  case_31: missing required field 'summary'
97	```
98	
99	Output is what convinces a reader the tool does what the description claims. An example without output asks for faith.
100	
101	Stop at three. A fourth example belongs in a docs page linked from here.
102	
103	## What belongs elsewhere
104	
105	Move out of the README, leaving a link:
106	
107	- Full API or CLI reference
108	- Architecture and internals
109	- Long troubleshooting catalogs
110	- Design rationale and history
111	- Extensive configuration for edge cases
112	
113	A README over roughly 300 lines has become a manual and has stopped answering the four questions. Split it into `docs/` and link from a short Documentation section.
114	
115	## Contributing guides
116	
117	Separate file, `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Cover only what a contributor cannot infer:
118	
119	- How to set up a development environment, as commands
120	- How to run tests, as a command
121	- Code style enforcement — the tool and how to run it, not a prose style essay
122	- Branch and commit message conventions, with one real example each
123	- What review looks like and how long it typically takes
124	
125	Skip the code of conduct summary, the pep talk, and the general git tutorial. Contributors capable of contributing already have those.
126	
127	## Changelogs
128	
129	`CHANGELOG.md`, newest first, grouped by release with a date. Within a release, group by *Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security*.
130	
131	Entries describe user-visible effect, not commits:
132	
133	- Good: `Fixed test case IDs being reassigned during bulk import.`
134	- Bad: `Refactored import handler (#412).`

# READMEs and Project Docs

## Contents

- What a README is for
- Standard structure
- The first screen
- Installation and configuration
- Usage examples
- What belongs elsewhere
- Contributing guides
- Changelogs
- Review checklist

## What a README is for

A README answers four questions for someone who arrived from a search result and will leave in thirty seconds if unsatisfied:

1. What is this?
2. Do I want it?
3. How do I run it?
4. Where do I go next?

It is not a manual. Every paragraph that does not serve one of those four questions pushes the answers below the fold.

## Standard structure

```
# project-name

<one-sentence description>

<badges — optional, and only informative ones: build, version, license>

## What it does
## Requirements
## Installation
## Quick start
## Configuration
## Documentation  (links out)
## Contributing
## License
```

Reorder only for a reason. Readers scan for these headings by habit, and unfamiliar organization costs them time.

## The first screen

The single most valuable line is the description directly under the title. It must be concrete and complete without context:

> An MCP server exposing TestLink test case management to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol.

Not:

> A powerful, flexible tool for modern test workflows.

Marketing adjectives — powerful, seamless, blazing fast, modern, simple — carry no information and signal that the author had nothing specific to say. Delete them all.

Follow the description with what the project does in three to six bullets, each naming a real capability. Then reach a runnable command as fast as possible. If a reader cannot execute something within the first screen, the README is too slow.

Badge rows exceeding four items become noise. Keep build status, version, and license; drop the rest.

## Installation and configuration

State prerequisites with versions before the install command, so a reader fails fast rather than midway:

```
Requires Python 3.11+, and a TestLink instance with the XML-RPC API enabled.
```

Give one canonical install path. Alternatives (source build, container, package manager variants) go below the canonical one, clearly subordinate. Presenting three equal options forces a decision the reader is not equipped to make.

Document configuration as a table, since readers arrive looking for one specific key:

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TESTLINK_URL` | Yes | — | Base URL of the TestLink XML-RPC endpoint |
| `TESTLINK_API_KEY` | Yes | — | Personal API key from user settings |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | No | `30` | Seconds before an API call aborts |

Never put a real credential in an example, even an expired one.

## Usage examples

Two or three examples, ordered by frequency of use, not by complexity. The first must be the thing almost everyone does.

Each example shows the invocation and its output:

```bash
testcase-validator check --project TestLink-QA --file cases.json
```

```
Validated 47 cases. 2 rejected:
  case_12: field 'importance' = 'critical' (expected: 1, 2, 3)
  case_31: missing required field 'summary'
```

Output is what convinces a reader the tool does what the description claims. An example without output asks for faith.

Stop at three. A fourth example belongs in a docs page linked from here.

## What belongs elsewhere

Move out of the README, leaving a link:

- Full API or CLI reference
- Architecture and internals
- Long troubleshooting catalogs
- Design rationale and history
- Extensive configuration for edge cases

A README over roughly 300 lines has become a manual and has stopped answering the four questions. Split it into `docs/` and link from a short Documentation section.

## Contributing guides

Separate file, `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Cover only what a contributor cannot infer:

- How to set up a development environment, as commands
- How to run tests, as a command
- Code style enforcement — the tool and how to run it, not a prose style essay
- Branch and commit message conventions, with one real example each
- What review looks like and how long it typically takes

Skip the code of conduct summary, the pep talk, and the general git tutorial. Contributors capable of contributing already have those.

## Changelogs

`CHANGELOG.md`, newest first, grouped by release with a date. Within a release, group by *Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security*.

Entries describe user-visible effect, not commits:

- Good: `Fixed test case IDs being reassigned during bulk import.`
- Bad: `Refactored import handler (#412).`

Mark breaking changes unmistakably at the top of the release, with the migration action stated inline.

## Review checklist

```
- [ ] Description under the title is concrete and standalone
- [ ] Zero marketing adjectives
- [ ] Prerequisites with versions appear before install
- [ ] A runnable command appears within the first screen
- [ ] Every command executed as written, from a clean environment
- [ ] Examples show output, not just invocation
- [ ] Configuration documented as a table
- [ ] No credentials, real or expired, in examples
- [ ] Under ~300 lines; deeper material linked out
- [ ] License stated
```

# Reworking the adoption unit — plan

Companion to `redesign-draft.md`, which is the design record for the six workflow units and
is not edited by this file. This one covers the seventh unit, the one the draft never had a
row for: `setup-agent-workflows`.

Last updated 2026-08-16.

## 1. Why it needs a rework, not a rename

The unit was built around an indirection the redesign removed.

```
DESIGNED (values indirection)              SHIPPED (defaults inline)
  unit ──reads──► project-profile.md         unit ──carries──► Values table + default
                        ▲                                            │
                setup writes the sections            overridden by   ▼   the project,
                                                          where it declares one
                                           platform ──derived at run time──► git remote
```

Its three stated jobs, against what shipped:

| # | Job as written | Still real? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the `project-profile.md` sections units resolve against | **No, for our units** | `gen-readme`, `open-pr`, `land-pr` and the rest state their own defaults and say the project's declaration wins |
| 2 | Bind the report contract in `CLAUDE.md` | **Broken as written** | The block it inserts cites `rules/agent-report.md`; this plugin ships no `rules/` directory |
| 3 | Find forked copies that shadow placed units | **Yes** | Confirmed live — see §3 |

**Restated goal.** Make a project's copy of the toolkit unambiguous: one copy of each unit,
and a stated override only where a unit's default is wrong for that project. Not a
profile-writing step.

Rename follows the restated goal and is decided last, once §2 and §3 are settled — the
name should describe the job that survives, and that job is not final yet.

## 2. Legacy artifacts — the evaluation

The recommendation on the table is *remove the story files and rule files*. Evaluated one
by one. Three agree, two do not.

| Artifact | Where | Recommendation | Verdict | The cost of the wrong call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/stories/` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done** at `8f47b2b`. Nothing writes or reads one | none |
| `plugins/**/rules/*.md` (5 files) | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** Each skill now carries its doctrine inline; a cited file with one reader rots unnoticed | none |
| `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` | this repo | remove | **AGREE — already done.** This repo declares no overrides | none |
| `templates/CLAUDE.md` | this repo | — | **CUT — byte-identical to the repo's own `CLAUDE.md`** after the staged edit. Two copies, one reader, no rule saying which is authoritative | a template that drifts from the file it was copied from |
| **the profile as a concept, in an adopter** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — keep the file, drop our sections** | §2.1 |
| **the `CLAUDE.md` binding** | adopter repos | remove | **PUSH BACK — replace, do not delete** | §2.2 |

### 2.1 The profile file survives us

Our six units no longer read it. `agent-workflows-runner` still does — it is placed from
`~/src/test-framework-template`, ships six `qa-*` commands plus `setup-agent-runner`, and
resolves `Paths`, `Reports`, `Connected flow` and its binding layer out of that same file.

| If we… | Then |
|---|---|
| delete the file from adopters | the runner's commands stop on an unresolvable value |
| keep writing our seven sections | we maintain a values layer nothing of ours reads |
| **stop owning sections, leave the file alone** | both plugins hold; ours use defaults, the runner keeps its own half |

There is one loose end either way. Every unit says *"the project's declaration wins"* without
naming where a declaration lives. Removing the file with no replacement leaves that sentence
unresolvable — the promise has to point somewhere, and `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` is

# Reworking the adoption unit — plan

Companion to `redesign-draft.md`, which is the design record for the six workflow units and
is not edited by this file. This one covers the seventh unit, the one the draft never had a
row for: `setup-agent-workflows`.

## 1. Why it needs a rework, not a rename

```
DESIGNED (values indirection)              SHIPPED (defaults inline)

                        ▲                                            │

                                                          where it declares one
                                           platform ──derived at run time──► git remote
```

| 2 | Bind the report contract in `CLAUDE.md` | **Broken as written** | The block it inserts cites `rules/agent-report.md`; this plugin ships no `rules/` directory |
| 3 | Find forked copies that shadow placed units | **Yes** | Confirmed live — see §3 |

and a stated override only where a unit's default is wrong for that project. Not a

---
name: remove-stale-files
description: |
  Finds and removes what earlier versions of this toolkit left in a project: forked
  commands and skills that shadow the placed units, rules and story files nothing reads
  any more, and the profile sections these units no longer resolve against. Shows every
  file before touching one, deletes only on a yes, and writes nothing back. A stale
  document an agent still reads costs more than the absent one it replaced.
when_to_use: |
  Use whenever one of the files below is read, edited, or about to be created. Its
  presence is the trigger; nobody has to ask for a cleanup. In `.claude/commands/`:
  `dw-story`, `dw-plan`, `dw-tasks`, `dw-implement`, `dw-create-pr`, `dw-merge`,
  `dw-review-story`, `dw-review-tasks`, `dw-review-implement`, `dw-review-pr`,
  `dw-test-design`, `qw-plan`, `qw-cases`, `qw-review-plan`, `qw-review-cases`,
  `qw-drift`. In `.claude/skills/`: `auditing-artifacts`, `auditing-readme`,
  `ship-create-pr`, `ship-merge`, `reviewing-finish`, `doc-gen-readme`,
  `doc-review-readme`, and a local copy of any name this plugin ships. In
  `.claude/rules/`: `agent-report.md`, `anti-slop.md`, `dev-workflow.md`,
  `doc-workflow.md`, `qa-workflow.md`, `ship-tail.md`, `profile-doctrine.md`, and the
  sections this plugin wrote into `project-profile.md`. Elsewhere: `docs/stories/`,
  `docs/agents/domain.md`, `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`,
  `CONTEXT.md`, and a `## How to report` or `## Agent skills` section in `CLAUDE.md` or
  `AGENTS.md`. Also on request: "clean up .claude", "why are there two ship-merge", "is
  this rule still read", "we retired that workflow, what is left". Not for a file the
  project wrote itself.
---

# Remove stale files

**A stale file is worse than a missing one.** A missing file sends an agent to the code. A
stale one answers, plausibly and wrongly, and nothing marks it as out of date. The cost
lands later, on whoever traces a bad decision back to a document that read as current.

So this unit deletes. It writes nothing, which is what makes it safe to run twice.

## The boundary

**Remove only what this toolkit wrote, or what shadows what it ships.** Everything else is
the project's, and a project's file is reported, never touched.

| Removable | Never |
|---|---|
| A local copy of a name this plugin ships | The project's own commands and skills |
| A unit this plugin shipped and retired | `docs/adr/`, and any document the project authored |
| A rule file this plugin shipped | `agent-workflows-runner`'s rules and profile sections |
| Sections this plugin wrote into `project-profile.md` | Foreign sections in that same file |
| Story files and agent notes this toolkit generated | Anything you cannot trace to this toolkit |

The two lists are [fork-migration.md](./fork-migration.md) for `.claude/commands/` and
`.claude/skills/`, and [stale-documents.md](./stale-documents.md) for the rest.

**When you cannot trace a file, it is the project's.** Say so and move on.

## Process

### 1. Detect

    ls .claude/commands/ .claude/skills/ .claude/rules/ 2>/dev/null
    ls docs/stories/ docs/agents/ 2>/dev/null
    grep -n '^## \(How to report\|Agent skills\)' CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null

Then read `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json`. A fork is only redundant if the
placed copy is really there, and `installed_plugins.json` pins an `installPath` into a
cache snapshot that may be many commits stale. On a `"source": "directory"` marketplace
that snapshot is not what loads at all.

Nothing found is a result. Report `CLEAN` and stop.

### 2. Show, and say the consequence

Name every file, and what replaces it. Say the unguessable parts **before** asking:

- **`qw-drift` has no replacement anywhere.** Removing it ends the project's drift
  detection; nothing in either plugin rebuilds it.
- **The runner is a separate placement.** Deleting `qw-*` where
  `agent-workflows-runner` is not placed leaves no QA half at all, not a renamed one.
- **A retired unit with no successor takes its capability with it.** That is the case to
  slow down on, because there is no new name to type in its place.

### 3. Ask

One question, covering the whole list. On no, remove nothing and report the shadowing as
`KEPT` — a fork the user chose to keep is a decision, not a failure.

### 4. Remove

Only the files named in step 2. In `project-profile.md`, delete this plugin's sections and
leave the file, its preamble, and every foreign section exactly as found.

### 5. Report

`CLEAN` · `REMOVED` · `KEPT`, in the two lines and a question of `reporting-outcomes`.

    REMOVED — 6 forks and 3 rule files; project-profile.md kept, foreign sections intact.
    Next: restart the session so the placed units load.
    Want the file list?

## Steps

Copy this checklist and tick each item as you finish it:

    Task Progress:
    - [ ] Detected: commands, skills, rules, docs, the CLAUDE.md sections
    - [ ] Each hit traced to this toolkit, or left alone as the project's
    - [ ] Consequences stated before the question
    - [ ] Asked once, for the whole list
    - [ ] Removed only what was named
    - [ ] Reported: CLEAN, REMOVED or KEPT

# Setup agent-workflows

**Placement puts the units where an agent loads them. This is the other half — adoption.**
The placed units describe *some* project; this makes them describe *this* one. It runs once
per repo, and again only to change an answer.

Three things, and the third is the one nobody expects to need:

- **Profile values** — the sections these units resolve against, so no unit stops on an
  unresolvable value
- **The report contract binding** — a line in `CLAUDE.md` that holds every session, rather
  than waiting for a skill to invoke itself
- **Fork migration** — the local copies of retired commands that still appear in the menu
  with nothing announcing which one ran

This is prompt-driven, not a script. Explore, present what you found, confirm, then write.

## It writes only what this plugin owns

A project may place several plugins that all read one `project-profile.md`. The rules are
in `profile-doctrine.md` → "More than one plugin writes this file", and they bind here:
own only what you read, add or update in place and never truncate, and treat a value
already there as a decision rather than something to overwrite.

The sections this plugin owns, and nothing else:

semantics.** See [profile-sections.md](./profile-sections.md).

If `agent-workflows-runner` is also placed, its sections — `Paths`, `ID schemes`, the test
front-matter contract, the project's binding and run layer — belong to **its** setup unit.

is there. Until the fork is gone, the namespaced form is the only one that says which copy
ran.

## The mapping

**Renamed** — the unit survived under a new name. The fork is redundant; delete it and
type the new name.

| Forked unit | Became |
|---|---|
| `dw-create-pr` | `ship-create-pr` (this plugin) |
| `dw-merge` | `ship-merge` (this plugin) |
| `qw-plan`, `qw-cases`, `qw-review-plan`, `qw-review-cases` | `qa-*` in **`agent-workflows-runner`** — a different plugin, placed separately |
| `auditing-artifacts`, `auditing-readme` | `reviewing-artifacts`, `reviewing-phrasing`, `reviewing-typography` (this plugin) |

**Deleted, not renamed** — this is the distinction easiest to get wrong. Nothing here has
a new name to type; the authoring half is no longer this plugin's.

| Forked unit | What replaces it |
|---|---|
| `dw-story`, `dw-plan`, `dw-tasks`, `dw-implement` | nothing here — the build half is out of scope |
| `dw-review-story`, `dw-review-tasks`, `dw-review-implement`, `dw-review-pr` | nothing — a diff review plus `reviewing-finish` cover it |
| `dw-test-design` | the runner's `qa-*` half |
| `qw-drift` | **nothing.** See the consequence below. |

**Rules** — these ship from the plugins now. A local copy of any of them drifts from the
one the units actually read.

| Forked rule | Ships from |
|---|---|
| `rules/agent-report.md`, `rules/profile-doctrine.md`, `rules/anti-slop.md` | this plugin |
| `rules/ship-tail.md`, `rules/doc-workflow.md` | this plugin |
| `rules/dev-workflow.md` | deleted with the pipeline it described |
| `rules/qa-workflow.md` | `agent-workflows-runner` |

**Keep.** `.claude/rules/project-profile.md` stays in the project — it is the values half
and it is the one file adoption edits. What changed is that its **doctrine preamble** now
ships as `profile-doctrine.md`; a project holding the old combined file should keep its
values and let the preamble shrink to the pointer, or the two drift.

## Consequences a project cannot anticipate

Say these out loud before removing anything — they are the reason this is a conversation
and not a delete loop.

- **`qw-drift` has no replacement.** Removing it orphans the project's drift tooling and
  whatever front-matter anchor that tooling read. If the project depends on drift
  detection, it keeps the fork or rebuilds it as a project-owned unit; nothing in either
  plugin will do it.
- **A local `project-profile.md` may be missing keys the surviving units read**, and may
  still carry the old combined form where the doctrine preamble sat inline. Keep its
  values; let the preamble shrink to the pointer, or the shipped `profile-doctrine.md` and
  the inline copy drift apart with nothing saying which one a unit followed.
- **The runner's units are a separate placement.** Deleting `qw-*` without placing
  `agent-workflows-runner` leaves the project with no QA half at all, not a renamed one.

## Telling what is actually placed

A fork is only redundant if the plugin's copy is really there, and the obvious way to
check is misleading.

`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` pins an `installPath` into a cache snapshot
that may be many commits stale — and on a **directory**-source marketplace that snapshot
is not what loads at all. Read `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json` first:

- `"source": "directory"` — the working tree at that path is what loads. Read the units
  there; a restart picks up uncommitted edits.
- `"source": "github"` — a snapshot pinned to a commit. `claude plugin update
  <plugin>@<marketplace>` moves it, and the commit is the version; there is no number to
  compare.

Qualify the name with the marketplace when updating — the bare plugin name does not
resolve.

---
name: remove-stale-files
description: |
  Finds and removes what earlier versions of this toolkit left in a project: forked
  commands and skills that shadow the placed units, rules and story files nothing reads
  any more, and the profile sections these units no longer resolve against. Shows every
  file before touching one, and deletes only on a yes. It never adds: every edit it makes
  is a removal. A stale document an agent still reads costs more than the absent one it
  replaced.
when_to_use: |
  Use whenever one of the files below is read, edited, or about to be created. Its
  presence is the trigger; nobody has to ask for a cleanup. In `.claude/commands/`:
  `dw-story`, `dw-plan`, `dw-tasks`, `dw-implement`, `dw-create-pr`, `dw-merge`,
  `dw-review-story`, `dw-review-tasks`, `dw-review-implement`, `dw-review-pr`,
  `dw-test-design`, `qw-plan`, `qw-cases`, `qw-review-plan`, `qw-review-cases`,
  `qw-drift`. In `.claude/skills/`: `auditing-artifacts`, `auditing-readme`,
  `ship-create-pr`, `ship-merge`, `reviewing-finish`, `doc-gen-readme`,
  `doc-review-readme`, and a local copy of any name this plugin ships. In
  `.claude/rules/`: `agent-report.md`, `anti-slop.md`, `dev-workflow.md`,
  `doc-workflow.md`, `qa-workflow.md`, `ship-tail.md`, `profile-doctrine.md`, and the
  sections this plugin wrote into `project-profile.md`. Elsewhere: `docs/stories/`,
  `docs/agents/domain.md`, `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`, `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`,
  `CONTEXT.md`, and a `## How to report` or `## Agent skills` section in `CLAUDE.md` or
  `AGENTS.md`. Also on request: "clean up .claude", "why are there two ship-merge", "is
  this rule still read", "we retired that workflow, what is left". Not for a file the
  project wrote itself.
---

# Remove stale files

**A stale file is worse than a missing one.** A missing file sends an agent to the code. A
stale one answers, plausibly and wrongly, and nothing marks it as out of date. The cost
lands later, on whoever traces a bad decision back to a document that read as current.

So this unit deletes. It writes nothing, which is what makes it safe to run twice.

## The boundary

**Remove only what this toolkit wrote, or what shadows what it ships.** Everything else is
the project's, and a project's file is reported, never touched.

| Removable | Never |
|---|---|
| A local copy of a name this plugin ships | The project's own commands and skills |
| A unit this plugin shipped and retired | `docs/adr/`, and any document the project authored |
| A rule file this plugin shipped | `agent-workflows-runner`'s rules and profile sections |
| Sections this plugin wrote into `project-profile.md` | Foreign sections in that same file |
| Story files and agent notes this toolkit generated | Anything you cannot trace to this toolkit |

The two lists are [fork-migration.md](./fork-migration.md) for `.claude/commands/` and
`.claude/skills/`, and [stale-documents.md](./stale-documents.md) for the rest.

**When you cannot trace a file, it is the project's.** Say so and move on.

## Process

### 1. Detect

    ls .claude/commands/ .claude/skills/ .claude/rules/ 2>/dev/null
    ls docs/stories/ docs/agents/ 2>/dev/null
    grep -n '^## \(How to report\|Agent skills\)' CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null

Then read `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json`. A fork is only redundant if the
placed copy is there, and `installed_plugins.json` pins an `installPath` into a
cache snapshot that may be many commits stale. On a `"source": "directory"` marketplace
that snapshot is not what loads at all.

Nothing found is a result. Report `CLEAN` and stop.

### 2. Show, and say the consequence

Name every file, and what replaces it. Say the unguessable parts **before** asking:

- **`qw-drift` has no replacement anywhere.** Removing it ends the project's drift
  detection; nothing in either plugin rebuilds it.
- **The runner is a separate placement.** Deleting `qw-*` where
  `agent-workflows-runner` is not placed leaves no QA half at all, not a renamed one.
- **A retired unit with no successor takes its capability with it.** That is the case to
  slow down on, because there is no new name to type in its place.

### 3. Ask

One question, covering the whole list. On no, remove nothing and report the shadowing as
`KEPT`: a fork the user chose to keep is a decision, not a failure.

### 4. Remove

Only the files named in step 2. In `project-profile.md`, delete this plugin's sections and
leave the file, its preamble, and every foreign section exactly as found.

### 5. Report

`CLEAN` · `REMOVED` · `KEPT`, in the two lines and a question of `reporting-outcomes`.

    REMOVED — 6 forks and 3 rule files; project-profile.md kept, foreign sections intact.
    Next: restart the session so the placed units load.
    Want the file list?

28	# Remove stale files
29	
30	**A stale file is worse than a missing one.** A missing file sends an agent to the code. A
31	stale one answers, plausibly and wrongly, and nothing marks it as out of date. The cost
32	lands later, on whoever traces a bad decision back to a document that read as current.
33	
34	So this unit deletes, and only deletes. Nothing it touches gains a line, which is what
35	makes it safe to run twice.
36	
37	## The boundary
38	
39	**Remove only what this toolkit wrote, or what shadows what it ships.** Everything else is
40	the project's, and a project's file is reported, never touched.
41	
42	| Removable | Never |
43	|---|---|
44	| A local copy of a name this plugin ships | The project's own commands and skills |
45	| A unit this plugin shipped and retired | `docs/adr/`, and any document the project authored |
46	| A rule file this plugin shipped | `agent-workflows-runner`'s rules and profile sections |
47	| Sections this plugin wrote into `project-profile.md` | Foreign sections in that same file |
48	| Story files and agent notes this toolkit generated | Anything you cannot trace to this toolkit |
49	
50	The two lists are [fork-migration.md](./fork-migration.md) for `.claude/commands/` and
51	`.claude/skills/`, and [stale-documents.md](./stale-documents.md) for the rest.

58	
59	    ls .claude/commands/ .claude/skills/ .claude/rules/ 2>/dev/null
60	    ls docs/stories/ docs/agents/ 2>/dev/null
61	    grep -n '^## \(How to report\|Agent skills\)' CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null
62

64	placed copy is there, and `installed_plugins.json` pins an `installPath` into a
65	cache snapshot that may be many commits stale. On a `"source": "directory"` marketplace
